defect.problem: The black-letter rule contains direct quotes and broad time/manner propositions that are not verifiable from the disclosed Jardines and King lake records, and no text files are present. The disclosed Jardines pinpoints support only the narrower drug-dog/curtilage search point; the disclosed King pinpoint supports only a general lawful-before-exigency framing, not the quoted occupant-obligation sentence.
defect.proposed_fix: Either supply full opinion text or verified lake pinpoints for Jardines pages 8 and 9-10 and King pages 469-70, or narrow the rule to the propositions actually present in the disclosed pinpoints.

reasons: No disclosed text/<case>.txt files exist for Jardines or King, so the page's quoted language cannot be checked for character fidelity or pin placement.

Jardines pin-6 says only that bringing a drug dog onto curtilage to gather evidence exceeds implied license and is a search; it does not verify the quoted front-path language or the full area/purpose/time/manner formulation.
King pin-op8 says the test keys on whether police acted lawfully before exigency arose; it does not verify the quoted statement that the occupant has no obligation to open the door or speak.
residual_risks: The broader black-letter rule may be legally accurate, but it is not proven by the disclosed evidence under this review protocol.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Separate verified SCOTUS text from lower-court gloss: state the Jardines dog/curtilage holding and King exigency premise, then add verified pinpoints before using the broader area/time/manner rule.
